adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — Async legacy writes derive their context from the request ctx, which is cancelled once the handler returns, so legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection can be aborted and the stores silently diverge.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection the legacy write is executed in a goroutine and the context used for the legacy call is derived from the incoming `ctx` (e.g. `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10*time.Second, ...) ... d.Legacy.Create(ctx, ...) }()`). Because the async context is a child of the request context (not detached via `context.Background()`), any cancellation of the parent `ctx` will immediately cancel the legacy operation, potentially preventing the legacy write while the unified-store write already succeeded—causing silent divergence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 — Legacy Create gets the original input obj instead of the object the unified store created, so generated name/UID/resourceVersion can differ between stores (generateName yields two different objects).

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, the unified store is called first (`created, err := d.Storage.Create(...)`), but the legacy write in the goroutine still uses the original input `obj` (`d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)`) rather than `created`. If `Storage.Create` assigns server-side fields (e.g., generated name/UID/resourceVersion), legacy and unified stores can end up with different object identities/metadata. This behavior is directly visible in the diff and matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139 — Removing the updateWrapper means legacy Update re-applies objInfo against legacy's own old object (with unified-store preconditions/RV), so it can conflict or produce a different result than unified storage.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the previous implementation computed the updated object once (by calling `objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` using the unified-store "old" object) and then wrapped `objInfo` in an `updateWrapper` so both the Storage and Legacy updates would use the same already-materialized updated object. The new code removes that and calls `d.Storage.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` and later `d.Legacy.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` in a goroutine. That means Legacy will re-run `UpdatedObject` against Legacy’s own "old" object, which can produce a different updated object or fail due to RV/precondition differences, leading to divergence between unified storage and legacy storage—exactly the concern in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — Fire-and-forget goroutines have no ordering, so a fast create->update->delete sequence can reach legacy out of order (e.g. an update after a delete, or a create recreating a deleted object).

adjudication.rationale: In mode3, legacy writes are now done asynchronously via uncoordinated goroutines: Create() spawns a goroutine for d.Legacy.Create, Delete() spawns one for d.Legacy.Delete, Update() spawns one for d.Legacy.Update, and DeleteCollection() spawns one for d.Legacy.DeleteCollection. There is no per-object serialization or ordering between these fire-and-forget goroutines, so rapid sequences on the same resource (create→update→delete, etc.) can reach the legacy store out of order (e.g., an earlier Create goroutine executing after a later Delete), causing the legacy store to become inconsistent (including recreating a deleted object). This ordering guarantee existed implicitly when legacy calls were synchronous before this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:56 — Legacy write failures are only recorded as a metric boolean and never logged, which removes the prior error logging and hides divergence between the stores.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes were changed from synchronous calls that logged on error (e.g., previous Create: `log.WithValues("object", created).Error(err, ...)`) to asynchronous goroutines with timeout (`context.WithTimeoutCause`) that only call `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...)` and do not log failures (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). This removes prior error logging and can reduce visibility into legacy/unified store divergence, but it’s primarily an observability/regression concern rather than a directly verifiable correctness break in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — The unified-store Create failure is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, which misattributes storage errors to legacy metrics.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Create(), the error path after d.Storage.Create(...) calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). This is a unified-store (Storage) failure but is recorded as a legacy duration metric, misattributing storage errors/latency to legacy metrics. The surrounding code uses recordStorageDuration for successful storage calls, reinforcing that this is an inconsistency/defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129 — The unified-store Update failure is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, which misattributes storage errors to legacy metrics.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, when `d.Storage.Update(...)` returns an error, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` inside the `if err != nil { ... }` block. This records a unified-store (storage) failure under the legacy-duration metric, misattributing the error. The call should be to `recordStorageDuration(...)` for storage failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — The legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded with recordStorageDuration, so legacy failures show up as storage metrics.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go DeleteCollection(), the async legacy path calls d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...) but then records the duration via d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). This mismaps legacy operation metrics into storage metrics (and also uses the legacy start time), so legacy failures/latencies will be attributed to storage. It should use recordLegacyDuration for the legacy call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 — The successful Delete metric passes the object name as the kind label, which gives the metric unbounded cardinality and the wrong label.
pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97 — Delete stores d.Log in the context instead of the enriched log, so downstream logs lose the name/kind/method values.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:53 — Legacy and storage mocks share one mock.Mock and none of the tests wait for the async goroutine or assert on legacy calls, so the tests stay green even if legacy is never written or the wrong store is called.

adjudication.rationale: The new Mode3 implementation performs legacy writes asynchronously (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection each start a `go func()` calling `d.Legacy...`), but the rewritten `dualwriter_mode3_test.go` does not wait for those goroutines and does not assert legacy calls occurred (no `m.AssertExpectations(t)` or call-count checks). Additionally, both `ls := legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `us := storageMock{m, s}` share the same `*mock.Mock`, so expectations like `m.On("Create", mock.Anything, mock.Anything, ...)` can be satisfied regardless of which wrapper invoked them, weakening verification that the correct store was called. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test-quality issue rather than a proven production bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:38 — The "unified store fails" Create case only sets a legacy expectation, so it passes only because the storage call hits that shared-mock expectation, not because a storage failure is actually tested.

adjudication.rationale: In TestMode3_Create, the "error when creating object in the unified store fails" case only sets an expectation on the shared *mock.Mock for method "Create" in setupLegacyFn (returning an error for failingObj) and does not set any storage expectation. Since both legacyStoreMock and storageMock wrap the same mock and both call m.Called("Create", ...), the Storage.Create invocation in Mode3 can satisfy the legacy expectation (it passes failingObj), causing the test to fail for the wrong reason and not actually exercise a storage-specific failure path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go:132 — The mode 3 integration tests reuse doPlaylistTests and never check that legacy storage received the async writes, so divergence between the stores would go unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go the newly added mode-3 integration subtests simply call doPlaylistTests(...) (same helper used for other modes) and add no mode-3-specific assertions about the legacy side effects, even though mode 3 behavior in dualwriter_mode3.go now performs legacy writes asynchronously in goroutines. If doPlaylistTests only validates the API-visible behavior, these new tests would not detect missed/failed legacy async writes, so store divergence could slip by.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Storage create failure is recorded as a legacy-duration metric instead of storage.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, the error path after `d.Storage.Create(...)` fails calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`, even though the failed operation is the *storage* create. This should record a storage-duration metric (e.g., `recordStorageDuration`) rather than a legacy-duration metric.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129 — Storage update failure is recorded as a legacy-duration metric instead of storage.
pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 — Delete success metric passes object name instead of options.Kind as the kind label.
pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — Legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded via recordStorageDuration, corrupting storage metrics.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go within DeleteCollection, the legacy store operation is run in a goroutine and its duration is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`, even though it measures the legacy call (`d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)`). This misattributes legacy latency/error metrics to storage metrics, corrupting storage metric data and omitting the corresponding legacy metric (`recordLegacyDuration`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — Background legacy writes derive from the request ctx, which is cancelled when the request returns, so legacy writes can be silently aborted (should use context.WithoutCancel).

adjudication.rationale: In Mode3 the legacy operations are now executed asynchronously in goroutines (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) using `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` where `ctx` is the request-derived context (`ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log)` earlier). Since the handler likely cancels the request context once the request returns, these background legacy writes can be cancelled immediately and never complete, causing silent loss of the intended dual-write behavior. This is directly visible in the diff: each `go func()` derives its context from the incoming `ctx` rather than using `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`/`context.Background()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139 — Legacy update re-applies the raw objInfo against legacy's old object instead of wrapping the storage result, so legacy can diverge from unified storage (previous updateWrapper logic dropped).

adjudication.rationale:
In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, the previous Update implementation computed the updated object once and used an updateWrapper so both Storage.Update and Legacy.Update would apply the same updated object (and Legacy.Update would be driven by the Storage result). The new code calls d.Storage.Update(...) and then asynchronously calls d.Legacy.Update(...) with the original objInfo (no wrapper tying it to the Storage result):

- Old: compute `updated := objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)`; wrap objInfo; call Storage.Update; then call Legacy.Update with wrapper updated=obj from Storage.
- New: call Storage.Update with raw objInfo; then `go ... d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)`.

This allows Legacy.Update to re-run UpdatedObject against legacy's state and potentially produce a different object than what was persisted in unified storage, causing divergence as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 — Goroutine passes the same obj to Legacy.Create while the returned object/obj may be mutated by the caller concurrently, a data race.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Create, after writing to Storage, the code launches a goroutine that calls d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...) using the same `obj` reference passed into Create. Because the goroutine may run after Create returns, the caller can concurrently access/mutate `obj` (and Legacy.Create itself may mutate it), creating a potential data race introduced by this diff’s async legacy write behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97 — Delete puts d.Log instead of the enriched log into ctx, dropping name/kind/method log values.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Delete, the code builds an enriched logger `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` but then sets the context with the base logger: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`. As a result, `d.Storage.Delete(...)` and the legacy goroutine receive a context that does not carry the intended name/kind/method values (any downstream `klog.FromContext(ctx)` logging will miss them). This is a concrete, diff-grounded issue, but it affects observability rather than correctness of delete behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Storage-create failure is recorded via recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, mislabeling metrics.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Create, the storage call is timed with `startStorage := time.Now()` and then on `d.Storage.Create` error the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. That clearly records a *storage* failure using the *legacy* duration metric, mislabeling metrics. The success path correctly uses `d.recordStorageDuration(...)`, so the error path is inconsistent and likely wrong.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — Legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go inside DeleteCollection, the async legacy delete goroutine measures `startLegacy := time.Now()` and calls `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)`, but then records the result with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`. This is clearly the legacy path and should record legacy metrics (e.g., `recordLegacyDuration`), so the finding matches the diff and indicates incorrect metric attribution/labeling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97 — Delete stores d.Log instead of the enriched `log` in ctx, unlike all sibling methods.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Delete(), the code builds an enriched logger `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` but then sets the context logger with `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `log`. This is inconsistent with sibling methods (Create/Get/List/Update/DeleteCollection), which store the enriched logger in the context, and it will drop the added key/value fields for any downstream code that relies on `klog.FromContext(ctx)` (e.g., Storage/Legacy implementations) even though the local `log` variable still logs correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — The fire-and-forget legacy-write goroutine (timeout ctx + timing + metric) is copy-pasted four times with inconsistent ordering; extract a helper.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy write is performed asynchronously via a very similar fire-and-forget goroutine pattern in multiple methods (e.g., Create, Delete, Update, DeleteCollection). The blocks all set up a timeout context, track start time, call Legacy.*, and record a duration metric, but the internal ordering varies between methods (e.g., startLegacy before/after WithTimeoutCause; defer cancel placement). This is a concrete maintainability issue introduced by the diff (copy-paste with inconsistency) and is reasonably addressed by extracting a helper, but it is not itself a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — Hard-coded 10s legacy timeout repeated as a magic number in four places; should be a named constant.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `time.Second*10` hard-coded repeatedly in `context.WithTimeoutCause(...)` for legacy calls in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection, but this is a maintainability/style nit (naming a constant) rather than a verifiable defect or substantial review issue in behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 — Legacy write errors in goroutines are silently discarded (only metric), losing the previous log-on-failure behavior and making divergence undebuggable.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, legacy writes were changed from synchronous calls with error logging to asynchronous goroutines (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection now `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.<op>(...); d.recordLegacyDuration(...) }()`). Unlike the previous code paths (which did `log.Error(...)` / `log.WithValues(...).Error(...)` on legacy failures), the new goroutines do not log `err` at all—only metrics are recorded—so legacy-write failures become much harder to diagnose from logs. This is an observability/debuggability regression grounded in the diff, not a directly verifiable functional correctness break since the legacy write was already non-fatal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:35 — Doc comments (Create/Update/DeleteCollection) still describe synchronous dual writes though legacy writes are now async best-effort.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the comments for Create/Update/DeleteCollection still imply the operation writes/deletes to both storages as part of the call (e.g., “writes to LegacyStorage and Storage”, “writes first to Storage and then to LegacyStorage”, “deletes from both …”). The implementation now performs the legacy operation in a goroutine with a timeout (best-effort) and returns based on the Storage result (e.g., Create spawns a goroutine for d.Legacy.Create; Update spawns for d.Legacy.Update; DeleteCollection spawns for d.Legacy.DeleteCollection). This is a real, diff-grounded documentation mismatch but not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:33 — mode3Str duplicates Mode3 as a hand-maintained string literal rather than deriving from the DualWriterMode value.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `const mode3Str = "3"` in `dualwriter_mode3.go` and uses it for log/metric labels (`WithValues("mode", mode3Str)` and in `record*Duration(..., mode3Str, ...)`). This is a hand-maintained string representation of the mode value and could drift if the underlying `Mode3` constant/value changes; deriving the string from the `DualWriterMode` value would avoid that maintenance risk. The claim that it "duplicates Mode3" specifically can’t be fully verified from the diff because the `Mode3` constant definition isn’t shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — Background legacy writes derive their context from the request ctx, which is cancelled once the handler returns, so legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection (also lines 110, 135, 163) will frequently fail with context canceled.

adjudication.rationale: In Mode3 the legacy writes are now done asynchronously in goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) using `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` where `ctx` is the incoming request context (after `klog.NewContext`). Since the derived context inherits cancellation from the parent, any cancellation of the request ctx will immediately cancel the background legacy operation, making `Legacy.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection` likely to return `context canceled` before completing. This can cause missed legacy writes and inconsistent dual-write behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 — Legacy write errors in the background goroutines (also lines 112, 139, 165) are never logged, silently swallowing divergence between stores.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes were changed to run in background goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). Inside those goroutines the returned error is only used to call d.recordLegacyDuration(...), and is otherwise discarded—there is no log.Error(...) call anymore (unlike the previous synchronous legacy calls which logged errors). This creates a real observability/regression concern (legacy divergence can occur without logs), but it does not by itself prove broken behavior since the primary operation still returns the unified-store result and metrics may be intended to track legacy failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Storage Create failure is recorded as a legacy duration metric instead of storage (same bug at line 129 for Update).

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, the unified store (storage) failure path records `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` immediately after `d.Storage.Create(...)` returns an error. That is mismatched: it should record a *storage* duration metric for a storage operation (and uses the storage start time). Similarly in `DualWriterMode3.Update`, when `d.Storage.Update(...)` fails, it calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` instead of `recordStorageDuration`. This is a real, diff-verifiable correctness issue in metrics reporting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — Legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded with recordStorageDuration, corrupting storage metrics and hiding legacy failures.

adjudication.rationale:
In `DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection`, the async legacy deletion path records its duration via `d.recordStorageDuration(...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)`:

```go
_, err := d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)
d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)
```

This will misattribute legacy delete-collection timing/failures to storage metrics, which can hide legacy issues and corrupt storage telemetry. The finding is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 — Delete success metric passes the object name as the kind label, producing wrong and unbounded-cardinality metric labels.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, after a successful `d.Storage.Delete(...)`, the code records the storage duration with `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`. In all other methods (and even in the error path in Delete) the third argument is `options.Kind`, implying this parameter is the `kind` label. Passing `name` (object identifier) will both mislabel the metric and create unbounded/high-cardinality labels.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139 — Legacy Update reuses the raw objInfo instead of wrapping the Storage result, so legacy recomputes the update against its own state and can diverge from Storage.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Update, the diff removes the prior logic that computed the updated object once from Storage state and wrapped objInfo (via updateWrapper) so both Storage and Legacy would apply the same updated object. The new code calls d.Storage.Update(..., objInfo, ...) and then asynchronously calls d.Legacy.Update(..., objInfo, ...) using the same raw objInfo, which allows Legacy to recompute the update against its own current state and potentially produce a different result than Storage. This matches the finding and is directly visible in the new Update implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 — The goroutine hands the same obj to Legacy.Create while the caller serializes the returned object, a potential data race on a shared mutable object.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Create, after `created, err := d.Storage.Create(...)` the function returns `created` to the caller but also starts a goroutine that calls `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` using the same `obj` value passed into Create. Since `runtime.Object` is typically a pointer to a mutable struct and Storage.Create may return the same instance it was given (or mutate it in place), Legacy.Create can concurrently mutate the same underlying object while the caller is using/serializing `created`, creating a real potential data race introduced by this async legacy write pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97 — Delete puts d.Log rather than the enriched log into ctx, so downstream logs lose the name/kind/method fields.
matched_golden_ids: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue states that Delete stores d.Log in the context instead of the enriched log with name/kind/method fields, causing downstream logs to miss those fields. This is the same underlying issue described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:31 — Legacy and storage share one mock and the legacy Create(input) expectation is matched first, so the test cannot tell whether Storage or Legacy served the synchronous create.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go, the legacyStoreMock and storageMock are both backed by the same *mock.Mock (m). In TestMode3_Create, expectations are set on the same method name "Create" twice: legacy uses m.On("Create", ..., input, ...) while storage uses m.On("Create", ..., mock.Anything, ...). Since Mode3.Create calls d.Storage.Create(ctx, obj, ...) synchronously with obj==input, that first call can satisfy the legacy expectation, making the test unable to distinguish whether the synchronous Create came from Storage vs Legacy. This is test-quality/verification weakness (and it’s compounded by not asserting expectations/call counts), not a production defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:41 — The "unified store fails" case registers its failure through setupLegacyFn on the shared mock, so the test is mislabeled and the storage-failure path passes only because of the shared mock.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go TestMode3_Create, the case named "error when creating object in the unified store fails" does not set setupStorageFn at all; instead it sets an expectation in setupLegacyFn: `m.On("Create", ..., failingObj, ...)`. Because both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` are constructed with the same underlying `*mock.Mock` (`m := &mock.Mock{}`) and the expectation is on the unqualified method name "Create", the Storage.Create call made first by Mode3 Create can satisfy that expectation. The test therefore passes due to the shared mock rather than accurately targeting the unified-store failure path, making the case mislabeled/ambiguous (a test correctness issue, not a product defect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:63 — No mode 3 write test (Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection) waits for or asserts the async legacy write, so the new dual-write behavior goes unverified and a missing legacy call would pass silently.

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, Mode3 write paths now perform legacy writes asynchronously in goroutines (`Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `DeleteCollection` all `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.<op>(...) ... }()`). In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, the Mode3 tests primarily assert only the returned object/error from the unified store call and do not synchronize with or assert the async legacy calls (no wait mechanism, no `m.AssertExpectations(t)` / call-count assertions). As a result, a regression where the legacy call is removed or never executed could still pass these tests silently (or run after the test ends).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:228 — The Delete and DeleteCollection tests return before the legacy goroutine runs against the shared mock, which makes the tests racy and can cause an unexpected-call panic after the test has finished.

adjudication.rationale: In Mode3, Delete and DeleteCollection now spawn a goroutine that calls the legacy store asynchronously (dualwriter_mode3.go: Delete starts `go func(){ d.Legacy.Delete(...) }()`, and DeleteCollection starts `go func(){ d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...) }()`). In the new tests (dualwriter_mode3_test.go), TestMode3_Delete and TestMode3_DeleteCollection only set up expectations for the unified Storage mock and do not set any expectations for Legacy.* calls, while both legacyStoreMock and storageMock share the same underlying `*mock.Mock` (`m := &mock.Mock{}`). Because the legacy goroutine may execute after the test returns, it can trigger an unexpected-call panic (no expectation) and/or race with test teardown, making the tests racy/flaky as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:163 — The legacy goroutine's context comes from the request ctx, so a cancelled request also cancels the legacy write, and no test covers a cancelled request ctx or legacy failure/timeout.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3, legacy writes are now done asynchronously with `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...) ... d.Legacy.<op>(ctx, ...) }()`, where the derived context is created from the request `ctx` captured from the handler (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). That means if the request context is cancelled, the legacy write context will also be cancelled immediately (timeout won’t help), potentially skipping best-effort legacy replication depending on intended semantics. Also, the newly added mode3 tests don’t cover request-cancellation behavior or legacy timeout/failure behavior; in fact, tests generally don’t assert the goroutine executed (no waiting/synchronization), so legacy failure/timeout paths aren’t exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Metrics are recorded under the wrong labels: storage failures in Create/Update go to the legacy series (lines 45 and 129), Delete passes name as kind (line 106), and the legacy DeleteCollection goes to storage (line 166); no test checks metrics.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple metric-recording mistakes in `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`: (1) `Create` records a *storage* failure with `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` using `startStorage` (should be storage series). (2) `Update` similarly records a storage failure via `recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)`. (3) `Delete` on success calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`, passing `name` where other calls pass `options.Kind` (label mismatch). (4) `DeleteCollection`’s goroutine for legacy deletion calls `d.recordStorageDuration(...)` instead of `recordLegacyDuration(...)`. The added tests in `dualwriter_mode3_test.go` assert returned objects/errors but do not validate metrics/labels at all, so these issues would go uncaught.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:65 — Tests pass empty options with no Kind and assert only return values, so log and metric labelling by options.Kind is never exercised.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3 methods, logging/metrics label values are derived from options.Kind (e.g., Create/Get/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection: `d.Log.WithValues("kind", options.Kind, ...)` and `record*Duration(..., options.Kind, ...)`). In the new tests, several calls pass empty option structs with no Kind set (e.g., Create uses `&metav1.CreateOptions{}`, Get uses `&metav1.GetOptions{}`, Delete uses `&metav1.DeleteOptions{}`, Update uses `&metav1.UpdateOptions{}`), and assertions only check returned objects/errors, not metric/log labels. Therefore, those label paths (non-empty Kind values and correct label wiring) are largely not exercised by the tests (though List/DeleteCollection do set Kind via TypeMeta in their options in this diff).
